title: Contract + Pricing Hedge Framework: Legal Redline Ops Runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise deals often request indemnity/liability deviations or broad DPA/MSA redlines. Right now these exceptions are handled ad-hoc by sales + legal, causing inconsistent pricing concessions, slow deal cycles, and untracked margin leakage. We need a repeatable operational playbook that ties redline risk tiers to standardized pricing hedges and fast-path approvals so Sales can respond within 24 hours and Finance/legal can enforce guardrails.

Goals:
- Define a 3-tier risk matrix for MSA/DPA redlines (Low / Elevated / High) based on indemnity, liability cap, data residency, and audit scope.
- Map each tier to a recommended pricing hedge: discount cap change, SLA credit cap, security add-on fee, or auto-approve threshold.
- Build an approval fast-path for low-risk items (auto-approve with templated clause), 24-hour SLAs for Elevated, and mandatory legal committee review for High.
- Provide a single-page runbook for Sales + Solutions Engineers with actionable scripts + email templates.
- Wire an exceptions dashboard that captures: reason, clause text, estimated ARR impact, approval path, and outcome.

Acceptance criteria:
- A published 2-page runbook in Confluence + Drive (link in comments)
- A scoring rubric that yields deterministic tier for 90% of incoming redlines (manual override allowed)
- A pricing hedge catalog with clear finance owner and P&L guardrails for each hedge type
- Integration plan for tracking in the Contract Exceptions dashboard and a small demo dashboard in Metabase

Proposed approach:
1) Create a Risk Matrix: enumerate clause-level signals (indemnity scope, third-party claims, liability cap multiplier vs ARR, IP carve-outs, export controls). Score weight for each signal and define tier thresholds.
2) Hedge Catalog: for each tier map to 1 primary and 1 fallback hedge (e.g., Elevated -> 6-month premium for security add-on OR limit SLA credit to 0.25% monthly). Quantify expected ARR/cost impact with sample scenarios.
3) Ops Runbook: stepwise triage play for Sales/CSEs, templates for clause suggestions, who to DM in Legal/Finance, and decision SLA timers. Include escalation matrix and rollback/renewal triggers.
4) Dashboard & Telemetry: modify existing Intake form to include clause text and automated scoring; track time-to-decision and realized margin change per exception.
5) Pilot: run pilot with 3 AE teams for 4 weeks, capture telemetry, and iterate.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Tighter auto-approve thresholds reduce friction but increase financial risk. Finance must sign off on numeric caps.
- Automated scoring can misclassify nuanced IP/regulated-clause language; need manual override with audit trail.
- Some large accounts will require bespoke terms; ensure playbook does not block bespoke negotiation but requires explicit executive approval.

Key stakeholders: Sales (AE leads), Legal (Contracts & Privacy), Finance (Revenue Ops), Solutions Engineering, Customer Success.
